scriptDescriptions.usage: Run a command with `npm run <name>`. Arguments after `--` pass through to that command.
scriptDescriptions.testSelectors: Run one Feature Behavior Test (FBT) with `npm run test:id -- FBT-018`; run one Feature with `npm run test:feature -- F-170`; run one Feature Set with `npm run test:feature-set -- FS-100`.
scriptDescriptions.testViewingFlags: Add `--headed` to show browser windows or `--ui` for interactive Playwright UI mode. UI-mode results are not recorded; `test:gate` rejects `--ui`.
scriptDescriptions.modeledWseFlags: Modeled water-surface elevation (WSE) commands accept `--extent=<id>` (default: `dangermond-preserve`; fast development extent: `jalama-gauge-reach`), `--water-years=2020-2022`, and `--force`. Stage 4 also accepts `--wse-polygon-method=<id>`. Stages 4 and 5 accept `--modeled-wse-method=<id>` to read another saved modeled WSE method; `pipeline:modeled-wse:m2-time-series` requires it.

commands.help: Prints this command reference with descriptions, selectors, and supported flags; it does not run another command.
commands.dev: Starts the creek visualization browser's Vite development server.
commands.lint: Checks application, test, configuration, runner, and data-pipeline source files with ESLint; it does not run tests or modify files.
commands.pipeline:acquire: Downloads and retains the browser publication pipeline's source snapshots; requires network access and does not publish browser-ready data.
commands.pipeline:publish: Rebuilds browser-ready creek visualization data from retained snapshots; uses no network and does not rerun acquisition or the modeled-WSE pipeline.
commands.pipeline:modeled-wse:acquire: Runs modeled-WSE Stage 0: acquires flowlines, United States Geological Survey 3D Elevation Program (USGS 3DEP) terrain, reach assignments, and modeled discharge.
commands.pipeline:modeled-wse:cross-sections: Runs Stage 1: derives terrain-based creek cross-sections, bed elevations, slopes, banks, and reviewed reach assignments.
commands.pipeline:modeled-wse:rating-curves: Runs Stage 2: converts cross-sections into per-segment WSE-to-discharge rating curves.
commands.pipeline:modeled-wse:time-series: Runs Stage 3: combines rating curves and modeled discharge into per-segment WSE time series.
commands.pipeline:modeled-wse:m2-time-series: Runs Stage 3 for Modeled WSE Derivation Method m2-multi-section-manning-depth (requires `--modeled-wse-method=m2-multi-section-manning-depth`): reuses the saved Stage 0–1 output and writes per-segment anchor WSE, junction depths, and junction beds under 03-time-series/m2-multi-section-manning-depth/; never touches m1 output.
commands.pipeline:modeled-wse:m3-time-series: Runs Stage 3 for Modeled WSE Derivation Method m3-flowline-profile-manning-depth (requires `--modeled-wse-method=m3-flowline-profile-manning-depth`): reuses the saved Stage 0–1 output, fits one channel centerline per flowline on the 1 m lidar with the raw lidar at the creek’s lowest point as the bed (road and railroad fills breached), and writes per-segment pool-filled anchor WSE, true junction depths, and beds under 03-time-series/m3-flowline-profile-manning-depth/; never touches m1 or m2 output or an older m3 version.
commands.pipeline:modeled-wse:m4-time-series: Runs Stage 3 for Modeled WSE Derivation Method m4-flowline-profile-variable-power-depth (requires `--modeled-wse-method=m4-flowline-profile-variable-power-depth`): m3 v2 on m3 v2’s channel with a steep-creek roughness (Ferguson & Recking 2025 variable-power law, D84 assumed from slope, blended from Manning’s n over 2–8% slope); refuses to run unless m3’s code still matches saved m3 v2, and writes under 03-time-series/m4-flowline-profile-variable-power-depth/; never touches m1–m3 output.
commands.pipeline:modeled-wse:m5-time-series: Runs Stage 3 for Modeled WSE Derivation Method m5-flowline-profile-jarrett-depth (requires `--modeled-wse-method=m5-flowline-profile-jarrett-depth`): m4 with Jarrett’s 1984 steep-creek roughness (n = 0.32 S^0.38 R^-0.16, no grain size) and the same blend; writes under 03-time-series/m5-flowline-profile-jarrett-depth/; never touches m1–m4 output.
commands.pipeline:modeled-wse:water-surface-polyg: Runs Stage 4: generates prepared water-surface polygon sets from terrain and WSE inputs.
commands.pipeline:modeled-wse:catalog-and-validat: Runs Stage 5: builds the modeled-WSE catalog and validation report; exits nonzero for default-method validation failures.
commands.pipeline:modeled-wse:all: Runs modeled-WSE Stages 0–5 in order and forwards all arguments to every stage; writes git-ignored pipeline working output under data/pipeline-working-output/ and does not publish browser-ready data.
commands.data-products:freeze-wse-polygons: Freezes WSE polygons m1-v1 from Stage 4 output into an append-only folder under data/data-product-versions/ with a zipped file geodatabase for ArcGIS, then adds it to data/data-product-version-registry.json; refuses if the version exists and never contacts ArcGIS. Uses the Data-Pipeline conda environment (override with `ARCGIS_PYTHON_ENV`).
commands.data-products:validate-wse-polygons: Reads the frozen WSE polygons m1-v1 file geodatabase back and compares feature counts, attributes, ring coordinates, and geometry validity with the Stage 4 source; exits nonzero on a failed check.
commands.data-products:freeze-modeled-wse-m2: Freezes modeled WSE m2-v1 (Modeled WSE Derivation Method m2-multi-section-manning-depth, Stage 3 output) into an append-only folder under data/data-product-versions/ (zipped file geodatabase with the per-segment anchor point and junction beds, Held WSE Intervals of the anchor WSE and both junction depths, raw hourly CSV zips, version.json), then adds it to data/data-product-version-registry.json; refuses if the version exists or the method code changed since Stage 3, and never contacts ArcGIS. Accepts `--trial-folder=<path> --only-tnc-comids=<ids>` for a scratch run. Uses the Data-Pipeline conda environment (override with `ARCGIS_PYTHON_ENV`).
commands.data-products:validate-modeled-wse-m2: Reads the frozen modeled WSE m2-v1 file geodatabase and raw hourly CSVs back and checks every anchor WSE, junction depth, rebuilt junction WSE, Creek Segment anchor point and junction bed, field type, and Held WSE Interval against the Stage 1 and Stage 3 source JSON, with expected counts taken from the output; accepts `--version-folder=<path>` and exits nonzero on a failed check.
commands.data-products:freeze-wse-polygons-m2: Freezes WSE polygons m2-v1 (height-above-nearest-drainage-fill v1 Stage 4 output, built from modeled WSE m2-v1) into an append-only folder under data/data-product-versions/ with a zipped file geodatabase (MultiPolygon Z layer: bucket bounds min_depth_m / max_depth_m are water depths, Z is the local bed reference), then adds it to data/data-product-version-registry.json; refuses if the version exists or the method code changed since Stage 4, and never contacts ArcGIS. Accepts `--dry-run-into=<new folder>`. Uses the Data-Pipeline conda environment (override with `ARCGIS_PYTHON_ENV`).
commands.data-products:validate-wse-polygons-m2: Reads the frozen WSE polygons m2-v1 file geodatabase back and compares feature counts, depth-named attributes, Z (bed reference) and ring coordinates, and geometry validity with the Stage 4 source, with expected counts taken from the Stage 4 manifest; exits nonzero on a failed check.
commands.data-products:freeze-modeled-wse-version: Freezes any version of a depth-style Modeled WSE Derivation Method (m2–m5) as its own Data-Product Version, for example `-- --method m4-flowline-profile-variable-power-depth --version m4-v1`: reads identity, change note, fingerprint, and anchor-point source from the Stage 3 manifest, writes an append-only folder under data/data-product-versions/ (zipped file geodatabase, raw hourly CSV zips, version.json), and adds the version to data/data-product-version-registry.json; an older version whose code has since changed is frozen from the git commit that holds it. Refuses an existing label and never contacts ArcGIS. Accepts `--trial-folder=<path> --only-tnc-comids=<ids>`. Uses the Data-Pipeline conda environment (override with `ARCGIS_PYTHON_ENV`).
commands.data-products:validate-modeled-wse-versi: Reads a frozen depth-style modeled WSE version back (`-- --method <id> --version <label>` or `-- --version-folder=<path>`) and checks every Held WSE Interval, monthly value, and raw hourly CSV value, the Creek Segment anchor point, beds, and null notes against the Stage 3 and anchor-source files; exits nonzero on a failed check.
commands.data-products:freeze-wse-polygons-versio: Freezes any version of a depth-bucket WSE Polygon Generation Method (height-above-nearest-drainage-fill or flowline-channel-ribbon) as its own Data-Product Version, for example `-- --method flowline-channel-ribbon --version m3-v2` (method number from the registry, version number from Stage 4): MultiPolygon Z layer with depth bucket bounds and the bed as Z, plus a per-segment channel_ribbons table for a ribbon; adds it to the registry, refuses an existing label, and never contacts ArcGIS. Accepts `--dry-run-into=<new folder>`.
commands.data-products:validate-wse-polygons-vers: Reads a frozen depth-bucket WSE polygon version back (`-- --method <id> --version <label>` or `-- --version-folder=<path>`) and compares every feature's attributes and rings (with Z), ring and vertex totals, geometry validity, and the channel_ribbons table with the Stage 4 source; exits nonzero on a failed check.
commands.data-products:publish-arcgis-version: Publishes one frozen Data-Product Version as its own private hosted feature layer named creek_water_visualization_<product>_<label> in the Creek Water Visualization folder, for example `-- --product modeled-wse --version m4-v1 --upload-raw-csv --publish`; prints the plan only without `--publish`, refuses already-published versions and taken service names, leaves every item owner-only and Query-only, never deletes portal items, and fills only that version's ArcGIS ids in the registry. Reads credentials from `ARCGIS_DOTENV_PATH` (default ../../Data-Pipeline/.env).
commands.data-products:verify-arcgis-version: Read-only check of one published Data-Product Version (`-- --product <product> --version <label> --output <file.json>`): every item private, the service Query-only, layer ids, row counts, and fields equal the frozen version, and a seeded sample of hosted values (modeled WSE) or rings (WSE polygons) equal the pipeline output; writes the findings as JSON and exits nonzero on a mismatch. Signs in with `ARCGIS_DOTENV_PATH`.
commands.data-products:freeze-wse-polygon-rings: Freezes the exact station-ordered rings of a frozen channel-ribbon WSE polygons version as a supplementary table, for example `-- --version m3-v2`, because ArcGIS splits self-crossing ribbon rings when the polygon layer is published: checks the Stage 4 files against the frozen manifest hashes and every ring against the frozen file geodatabase, writes data/data-product-versions/wse-polygons/<method>/<label>-rings/, refuses an existing folder, and never contacts ArcGIS. Accepts `--trial-folder <folder>`.
commands.data-products:publish-wse-polygon-rings: Publishes the frozen exact-ring table of a channel-ribbon WSE polygons version as its own private, Query-only service named after the version's service plus `_rings`, for example `-- --version m3-v2 --publish`; prints the plan only without `--publish`, refuses a taken service name, never deletes portal items, and adds the ids to the version's registry entry as `arcgis.exact_rings_service`.
commands.data-products:share-default-pairing-serv: Shares the three services the production build opens by default with Everyone (modeled WSE m5-v1, WSE polygons m3-v2, and its exact-rings service), puts a plain-language description above the technical one, saves the public item text in arcgis-publishing/item-metadata/, and records `public_sharing` in the registry; leaves file geodatabase and CSV items, m1-v1, and every other version untouched. Prints the plan and current sharing only without `--publish`; `--output <file.json>` writes the before/after record.
commands.data-products:publish-arcgis: Publishes one frozen data-product version to ArcGIS Enterprise as a private hosted feature layer in the Creek Water Visualization folder, for example `-- --product wse-polygons --version m1-v1 --publish`; prints the plan only without `--publish`, refuses already-published versions and taken service names, and never deletes portal items. Reads credentials from `ARCGIS_DOTENV_PATH` (default ../../Data-Pipeline/.env).
commands.data-products:freeze-modeled-wse: Freezes modeled WSE m1-v1 from the Stage 0–3 working output into an append-only folder under data/data-product-versions/ (zipped file geodatabase for ArcGIS, raw hourly CSV zips, version.json), then adds it to data/data-product-version-registry.json; refuses if the version exists and never contacts ArcGIS. Uses the Data-Pipeline conda environment (override with `ARCGIS_PYTHON_ENV`).
commands.data-products:validate-modeled-wse: Reads the frozen modeled WSE m1-v1 file geodatabase and raw hourly CSVs back and checks every value, junction series, Creek Segment count, and field type against the Stage 3 source JSON; accepts `--version-folder=<path>` and exits nonzero on a failed check.
commands.data-products:verify-hosted-modeled-data: Runs the browser's hosted ArcGIS adapters against the live published modeled WSE and WSE polygon services (read-only queries) and compares the rebuilt Time Series, polygon sets, reach crosswalk, and Creek Segment paths with the local dangermond-preserve pipeline working output; exits nonzero on a mismatch. Gets a short-lived token through the Data-Pipeline conda environment (override with `ARCGIS_PYTHON_ENV`) and `ARCGIS_DOTENV_PATH` (default ../../Data-Pipeline/.env); the token is kept in memory only.
commands.data-products:verify-hosted-default-mode: Runs the browser's hosted ArcGIS adapters against the live services the production build opens by default (modeled WSE m5-v1, WSE polygons m3-v2 and its exact-rings service; read-only queries) and compares every rebuilt hourly Time Series file the hosted version publishes, every ribbon polygon set file (every vertex with its bed z), the default method pairing, the catalog, the reach crosswalk, and the Creek Segment paths with the local dangermond-preserve working output; reports expected differences by name and exits nonzero on a mismatch. `-- --anonymous` sends no token (the services must be public); otherwise a short-lived token comes from the Data-Pipeline conda environment and is kept in memory. `-- --flowlines <comid,…>` checks a subset.
commands.data-products:verify-hosted-observed-dat: Runs the browser's hosted observed-gauge adapter against the live public Creek Gauge Data, modeled WSE (Creek Segments), and WSE polygon services (read-only queries, no sign-in) and compares the rebuilt Jalama Near Lompoc Time Series, gauge-segment polygons, and Creek Segment paths with the shipped files in public/published-creek-visualization-data; also reports Provisional and Approved reading counts and exits nonzero on a mismatch.
commands.test:fast-only: Runs enabled non-browser tests marked fast across all test categories; excludes browser tests.
commands.test:features: Runs every enabled FBT, including required and nonblocking tests; excludes Critical Core and Supporting Tests.
commands.test:core: Runs every enabled Critical Core Test (CCT) only.
commands.test:shared: Runs every enabled Shared Supporting Test (SST) only; these tests are advisory and never release-blocking.
commands.test:browser-deterministic: Runs enabled browser tests with controlled network inputs; unexpected external requests fail.
commands.test:browser-live: Runs enabled live-service browser tests against cached-or-live external map and terrain services.
commands.test:refresh-map-cache: Deletes cached Esri and USGS 3DEP responses, then runs every enabled live browser test to refill the cache.
commands.test:browser-all: Runs every enabled browser test in deterministic and live modes; excludes non-browser tests.
commands.test:gate: Runs required CCTs, then required FBTs, stopping on a blocking failure or inconclusive result; excludes Supporting Tests and lint.
commands.test:all: Runs every enabled catalog test plus lint, then reports release eligibility separately from overall diagnostic health.
commands.test:view-test-catalog: Writes and serves the static human-facing test catalog without running tests; accepts `--no-open`, `--no-serve`, and the `TNC_CATALOG_PORT` environment variable.
commands.test:feature: Runs enabled tests associated with one Feature, for example `npm run test:feature -- F-170`; a Feature Behavior, Critical Core, Feature Supporting, or Shared Supporting Test identifier instead runs that single test even when disabled.
commands.test:id: Runs exactly one catalog test by identifier, for example `npm run test:id -- FBT-018`; explicitly selected disabled tests also run.
commands.test:feature-set: Runs enabled tests associated with one Feature Set, for example `npm run test:feature-set -- FS-100`.
